SAME IMPORT BOUNDARY, content-addressed: the content-addressed closure cache (graduate --env olean warm load) materializes the SAME definitional constants, from the SAME .olean set, that load_register.rs registers via this exact hook — the cache only changes the source of the bytes (a blake3-union-digest-bound, per-constant-recon-digest-stamped .mathverse shard) not the trust. Constants stored Unverified; every graduation candidate is re-type-checked from scratch downstream (graduate_with_base_keep_env -> add_decl check_type), so a wrong cached byte fails a candidate's recheck, it cannot mint a KernelVerified. Fail-closed: any union-digest / per-shard-binding / coverage / decode mismatch falls back to the eager .olean reconstruction. Opt-in via $CLEAN_CLOSURE_CACHE_DIR (off by default).

SOUND AS TRUSTED CLOSURE CONTEXT (2026-07-08, gate green-up after the P4 per-constant-verify landing left 2 unaccounted sites): fn insert_or_upgrade demand-loads the transitive CONSTANT closure of a per-constant-verify target into the shared kernel environment (2 call sites: the stale-entry re-insert arm and the fresh-insert arm). Closure constants are imported CONTEXT, trusted exactly like the eager import closure `stamp-verified --closure-root` loads: they are never stamped KernelVerified, never certified, and never enter a trust receipt. Only the named TARGET constant(s) run the kernel's add_decl-equivalent check_type gauntlet, and only kernel-accepted targets become receipt leaves. A corrupt or wrong closure constant can at worst fail the target's kernel check (fail closed) - it cannot mint a false KernelVerified or widen any certified claim.
